instruction: Dynamic Component with height attribute Build a SketchUp-style "ParametricTower" Dynamic Component whose height is driven by a `LenZ` attribute, then export the *default instance* (LenZ = 5 m) to COLLADA. Serialize the AttributeDictionary either in a sidecar JSON file or in an embedded `<extra>` block. Specification: 1. Component name: `ParametricTower` - this name must appear as the value of the `name` (or `id`) attribute on the single `<node>` in the visual scene, on the `<geometry>` element, and on the `component_name` value inside the SketchUp `<extra>` block (if you emit one). 2. Geometry: a closed axis-aligned rectangular prism, horizontal footprint 2 m x 2 m, vertical height = the value of the `LenZ` dynamic attribute (i.e. 5 m for the default instance). The prism's bottom face must sit on z = 0 (the `LenZ` attribute is a pure height, not a top-face Z). X and Y footprint may be centred on the origin or anchored at the origin corner - XY position is unconstrained as long as the spans are correct. 3. Dynamic attribute: a SketchUp Dynamic Component stores user-editable parameters in an `AttributeDictionary` named `dynamic_attributes` (see `[SU-Dynamic]` and `[SU-Ruby] AttributeDictionary`). For this task the dictionary must contain at least: - `LenZ` (float, meters, default = 5.0) - the height driver. You may additionally record `LenX`, `LenY`, and the SketchUp form-field helpers (`_LenZ_label`, `_LenZ_min`, `_LenZ_max`, `_LenZ_units`, `_LenZ_formlabel`, `_LenZ_access`) - they are optional. 4. Serialize the AttributeDictionary using EITHER of the following (at least one is mandatory): (a) An `<extra>` element inside the `<node>` for `ParametricTower`, containing `<technique profile="SketchUp">` wrapping `<attribute_dictionary name="dynamic_attributes">` with one `<attribute name="..." type="...">VALUE</attribute>` child per key. Recognised type hints: `int`, `float`, `bool`, `string`. (b) A sibling file `attributes.json` placed alongside `C:\Users\user\Desktop\output.dae`, either flat (`{"LenZ": 5.0,...}`) or nested (`{"dictionaries": {"dynamic_attributes": {"LenZ": 5.0}}}`). If both are present, their `LenZ` values must agree. 5. Units: meters; the DAE `<asset>` block should declare `<unit name="meter" meter="1.0"/>`. The up-axis is `Z_UP` (consistent with SketchUp world axes). Write the DAE to `C:\Users\user\Desktop\output.dae`. If you use the sidecar route (4b), also write `attributes.json` to the same directory. Requirements: 1. `C:\Users\user\Desktop\output.dae` exists and parses as well-formed XML / COLLADA. 2. DAE contains >= 1 geometry with >= 8 position vertices (a closed box). 3. Bounding-box X span approx 2.000 m (tolerance +/-10 mm). 4. Bounding-box Y span approx 2.000 m (tolerance +/-10 mm). 5. Bounding-box Z span approx 5.000 m (tolerance +/-10 mm) - must match LenZ. 6. Bounding-box z_min approx 0 (tolerance +/-10 mm): the tower's base sits on the ground plane. 7. A `dynamic_attributes` dictionary is present either (a) as a `<extra><technique profile="SketchUp"><attribute_dictionary name="dynamic_attributes">` block inside the DAE, or (b) as an `attributes.json` file in the same directory. 8. `LenZ = 5.0` is recorded in whichever of those channels is used (tolerance 1e-3). 9. If both the DAE `<extra>` block and `attributes.json` are present, their `LenZ` values must agree (tolerance 1e-3). 10. The geometry Z span matches the *recorded* LenZ to within 10 mm - geometry and attribute must not disagree. [Software] Launch SketchUp with `C:\SketchUp 2026 26.0.429 x64 En Portable\SketchUp.exe` (adjust if your install differs).
